broader_review_uses.material: 肠道-肿瘤轴（Gut-Tumor Axis）的概念，包括肠道屏障功能、全身炎症、代谢物转运（SCFA, LPS, TMAO）及其对远处器官（如乳腺组织）免疫微环境的影响。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 概念框架

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 展示可修饰的生活方式和医疗实践对免疫治疗结果的潜在影响，为讨论个体化治疗和预防策略提供依据。
broader_review_uses.material: 肥胖和抗生素使用作为常见的环境因素，如何通过改变微生物群组成进而影响TNBC预后和治疗反应。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 对比情境

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提醒在综合现有证据时需考虑研究质量和技术变异性，避免过度解读观察性关联；强调未来研究需要标准化协议和前瞻性设计。
broader_review_uses.material: 当前微生物组研究的方法学异质性（采样方法、测序平台、数据分析）、样本量小、混杂因素多，以及微生物群干预的安全风险（如FMT的感染风险）。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 局限性警示

facet_contributions.boundaries: 证据主要来自回顾性分析和特定试验的子集分析；因果关系尚未确立；不同研究间微生物组测序方法和分析流程的差异可能导致结果不可直接比较。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群特征（特别是高Alpha多样性和产SCFA菌群富集）与TNBC患者对免疫检查点抑制剂（如atezolizumab联合化疗）更好疗效（延长PFS、提高pCR）的临床关联证据。引用了ALICE试验的分析结果，指出高PD-L1表达与高微生物多样性协同预测最佳获益。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于支持“微生物群特征可作为ICI疗效预测生物标志物”的观点；展示微生物群与免疫治疗相互作用的临床重要性。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 许多机制细节基于小鼠模型或体外研究；人体内的确切通路仍需更多验证；不同微生物物种的具体作用可能存在重叠或拮抗，文中未完全区分所有细微差别。
facet_contributions.contribution: 详细描述了微生物群调节ICI疗效的潜在机制：1) 有益菌（如Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium）通过产生SCFA增强树突状细胞成熟、CD8+ T细胞活化和M1巨噬细胞极化；2) 有害菌/失调状态通过LPS易位激活TLR4信号，诱导M2型巨噬细胞和免疫抑制微环境；3) 抗生素通过减少淋巴细胞计数削弱全身免疫监视。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释微生物群影响免疫治疗响应的生物学基础；连接全身炎症、肠道屏障完整性与局部肿瘤免疫微环境的变化。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 干预措施的有效性和安全性在TNBC人群中尚未得到充分验证；FMT存在感染和耐药基因传播风险；饮食干预的具体方案和长期效果未知。
facet_contributions.contribution: 探讨了基于微生物群的干预策略（饮食、益生菌、FMT）在优化TNBC治疗中的潜力和挑战。指出目前证据多为前临床或外推自其他癌症类型，缺乏TNBC特异性的随机对照试验数据。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于讨论当前微生物群靶向疗法的转化医学障碍和未来研究方向；强调需要设计严谨的临床试验来验证这些策略。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤（特别是TNBC）对免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的反应提供了重要的机制背景和临床关联证据。它详细阐述了有益菌代谢物（如SCFA）和有害菌产物（如LPS）如何通过全身循环影响肿瘤微环境的免疫状态，并提供了抗生素使用、肥胖等可修饰因素对治疗结果的实证关联。对于综述中关于“微生物群如何调节ICI疗效”及“中介机制”的问题，本文提供了从分子机制到临床表型的多层次素材，特别是关于多样性、特定菌属与PFS/pCR关联的数据，以及FMT、饮食干预等未来方向的评估。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 本文是叙事性综述，非系统性综述，其结论代表作者对现有文献的综合解读，而非经过严格统计合成的定量结果。
所引用的临床关联数据（如抗生素与生存期的关系）主要来自回顾性队列，存在潜在的混杂偏倚，不能直接推断因果关系。
机制描述多基于动物模型或体外实验，其在人体TNBC患者中的适用性和效力需谨慎评估。
关于种族差异的讨论目前缺乏直接证据，仅为假设性推测，不应视为既定事实。
微生物群干预措施（如FMT、益生菌）在TNBC中的安全性和有效性尚未确立，仍处于实验阶段。
topic_handles: immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response in TNBC
fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) safety and efficacy

study_summary_A.approach: 采用叙事性综述方法，系统梳理和综合现有的流行病学数据、临床观察研究、动物模型实验结果以及体外机制研究。作者通过分类讨论有益微生物（如产短链脂肪酸菌）和促肿瘤微生物的功能，分析肠道-肿瘤轴（Gut-Tumor Axis）的机制路径（包括代谢物转运、免疫细胞调控、屏障功能破坏），并评估不同干预策略的证据等级和临床可行性。未进行系统性文献检索或Meta分析。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了TNBC背景下肠道微生物群与免疫治疗反应的综合性机制框架，特别强调了“肠道-肿瘤轴”在全身免疫调节中的作用。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 作为叙事性综述，缺乏系统性检索和定量合成；所引用的证据多为观察性关联或前临床模型，因果关系的确定性有限；未提供具体的临床试验设计细节或标准化方案。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 明确了抗生素滥用对TNBC预后的负面影响及其潜在的免疫介导机制，提出了抗生素管理作为即时可行的临床策略。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 主要基于回顾性队列研究（如Ransohoff et al.）的相关性数据，混杂因素（如疾病严重程度、合并症）的控制情况需结合原文仔细评估。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 识别了种族差异、肥胖等社会决定因素与微生物群变化的潜在交互作用，指出了该领域知识空白。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 关于种族/民族特异性微生物组与TNBC结局的直接证据不足，目前多为推测性讨论。

key_findings.conditions: 高肠道微生物多样性及产短链脂肪酸（SCFA）菌群富集
key_findings.finding: 与TNBC患者对新辅助化疗和免疫检查点抑制剂更高的病理完全缓解率（pCR）、更长的无进展生存期（PFS）以及更活跃的抗肿瘤免疫微环境（如CD8+ T细胞浸润增加）相关。

key_findings.conditions: 肠道菌群失调（Dysbiosis），特别是由肥胖、抗生素暴露引起
key_findings.finding: 导致慢性低度炎症、免疫抑制、肠道屏障破坏（LPS易位），并与TNBC较差的总生存期和疾病特异性生存期相关；抗生素使用每增加一个月，死亡风险比（HR）增加5%。

key_findings.conditions: 特定有益菌（如Akkermansia muciniphila, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii）
key_findings.finding: 通过产生SCFA、维持肠道屏障、增强树突状细胞成熟和T细胞活化，促进抗肿瘤免疫反应，提高免疫治疗疗效。

key_findings.conditions: 特定有害菌（如Escherichia coli, Fusobacterium nucleatum）
key_findings.finding: 产生基因毒素、破坏上皮屏障、促进促炎微环境，与肿瘤进展、转移和不良预后相关。

key_findings.conditions: 肿瘤内微生物群（Intratumoral microbiome）
key_findings.finding: TNBC肿瘤内部存在独特的微生物群落，可能通过血液传播或局部入侵定植，直接调节局部TME和免疫反应，但其具体组成和功能仍在探索中。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 1. 肠道微生物群如何影响TNBC的生物学行为和治疗反应？2. 哪些微生物特征或代谢产物与更好的预后或对免疫治疗的响应相关？3. 肥胖、抗生素使用等环境因素如何通过改变微生物群影响TNBC结局？4. 基于微生物群的干预措施在TNBC管理中有哪些潜在应用和价值？
study_summary_A.research_scope: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC); gut microbiome composition and diversity; intratumoral microbiota; systemic inflammation and immune regulation; response to chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs).
study_summary_A.work_summary: 这是一篇关于肠道微生物群在三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）中作用的叙事性综述。文章旨在阐明肠道微生物如何通过调节宿主免疫、代谢和炎症状态，影响TNBC的发病风险、肿瘤微环境（TME）特征以及对化疗和免疫检查点抑制剂的治疗反应。综述整合了流行病学证据、机制研究（包括有益菌与促肿瘤菌的作用）、抗生素暴露的影响以及基于微生物群的干预策略（如饮食调整、益生菌、粪便微生物移植FMT等），并讨论了当前研究的局限性和安全性考量。

source_materials.title: Beyond the tumor: the role of the gut microbiome in triple-negative breast cancer

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供微生物组代谢产物（SCFAs, Indoles等）作为关键介导分子的实例。
broader_review_uses.material: 摘要中提到的SCFAs、吲哚衍生物、甲酚衍生物、氧化三甲胺等代谢物的变化及其与疗效的相关性。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 在综述中列举具体的微生物代谢物类别，说明它们可能是连接微生物组与宿主免疫系统的化学信使。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供抗生素使用对免疫治疗影响的临床证据。
broader_review_uses.material: DLBCL患者中特定抗生素与CAR-T疗效负相关的临床观察结果。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为临床实践中需要关注的混杂因素或负面干预措施的例子，强调微生物组保护策略的重要性。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 研究对象是CAR-T细胞而非内源性T细胞或ICIs作用下的T细胞；需区分外源性细胞治疗与内源性免疫应答的差异。不能直接推断该机制完全等同于ICIs起效的机制，但可作为旁证或类比机制。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了微生物代谢物（SCFAs）直接增强免疫细胞（CAR-T）代谢适应性和功能的具体实验证据。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 可用于解释肠道微生物组如何通过提供必需代谢物来支持免疫细胞的效能，进而影响抗肿瘤免疫反应。这有助于构建“微生物代谢物作为免疫调节剂”的机制框架。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 主要结论针对CAR-T，而非固体瘤中的ICI。不能直接用于回答ICI在实体瘤中的具体调制方式，仅能提供微生物组-免疫治疗相互作用的普遍性原则支持。
facet_contributions.contribution: 展示了抗生素干扰微生物组后对免疫治疗疗效的负面影响，强调了微生物组完整性对免疫治疗成功的重要性。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 可作为反面案例或背景信息，说明破坏微生物组平衡会削弱免疫治疗（包括潜在的ICI疗效）的效果，从而间接支持维持微生物组健康对ICI疗效重要性的论点。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文提供了关于微生物组代谢产物（特别是短链脂肪酸）调节免疫细胞（此处为CAR-T，但机制可类比于其他免疫细胞）功能的具体分子证据。虽然其主要关注点是CAR-T而非检查点抑制剂（ICIs），但其揭示的“微生物代谢物-免疫细胞代谢适应性-抗肿瘤效应”这一机制链条，对于理解肠道微生物组如何普遍性地调制抗肿瘤免疫反应具有重要参考价值，可作为解释微生物组影响免疫治疗疗效的潜在机制素材。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该研究聚焦于CAR-T细胞疗法，而非用户综述核心关注的免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）。在引用其机制时，必须明确指出这是在外源性CAR-T细胞上的发现，内源性T细胞对相同代谢物的响应可能不同。
该研究主要涉及血液肿瘤（DLBCL），而用户综述包含固体瘤。微生物组在血液肿瘤与固体瘤微环境中的作用可能存在差异，需谨慎外推。
摘要未提供详细的统计分析细节，因此关于“相关性”的强度及因果推断的稳健性需保持谨慎，避免过度解读为确凿的因果关系。

study_summary_A.approach: 采用多阶段混合研究设计：1. 回顾性临床观察：分析大型DLBCL患者队列（n=422）中不同类别抗生素使用与CAR-T生存预后的关联；2. 代谢组学探索：在发现集（n=67）和验证集（n=58）中评估抗生素对肠道/血液代谢组（如SCFAs、吲哚衍生物等）的影响；3. 体内机制验证：利用免疫健全的小鼠CAR-T模型，模拟抗生素暴露，评估系统性代谢紊乱及CAR-T疗效变化；4. 体外/离体机制补充：验证SCFAs对CAR-T细胞代谢适应性及功能的直接影响。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 建立了特定广谱抗生素暴露、肠道微生物组代谢输出减少（特别是SCFAs）与CAR-T疗效受损之间的临床和机制联系。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的统计调整变量（如疾病分期、既往治疗线数等）；未提供详细的抗生素给药时机与CAR-T输注的时间间隔数据；小鼠模型与人类复杂临床环境的转化差异未在摘要中详述。

key_findings.conditions: DLBCL患者接受抗CD19 CAR-T治疗前，使用具有厌氧菌覆盖能力的广谱抗生素（如哌拉西林-他唑巴坦、美罗培南）。
key_findings.finding: 与使用其他类别抗生素相比，此类抗生素暴露与患者较差的CAR-T生存预后显著相关。

key_findings.conditions: 在发现子集（n=67）和外部验证队列（n=58）中检测肠道和血液代谢物。
key_findings.finding: 上述抗生素使用与显著的肠道微生物组功能失调相关，表现为短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）、吲哚和甲酚衍生物以及氧化三甲胺等代谢物的显著降低。

key_findings.conditions: 免疫健全小鼠模型中给予美罗培南并进行抗CD19 CAR-T治疗。
key_findings.finding: 美罗培南诱导的系统性代谢紊乱（dysmetabolome）导致小鼠体内CAR-T疗效下降。

key_findings.conditions: 体外或机制层面评估SCFAs对CAR-T细胞的作用。
key_findings.finding: SCFAs能够增强CAR-T细胞的代谢适应性（metabolic fitness），从而改善其肿瘤杀伤能力。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 明确广谱抗生素暴露导致的肠道微生物组功能失调及其代谢产物改变，是否以及如何损害CAR-T细胞疗法在血液恶性肿瘤中的疗效。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 研究对象为弥漫大B细胞淋巴瘤（DLBCL）患者及CAR-T细胞治疗；研究情境涉及广谱抗生素（特别是具有厌氧菌覆盖能力的哌拉西林-他唑巴坦和美罗培南）的使用对肠道微生物组功能、代谢组学特征及CAR-T疗效的影响。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本研究旨在探究抗生素诱导的肠道微生物组失调如何影响嵌合抗原受体T细胞（CAR-T）疗法的临床结局。研究团队首先在大样本（n=422）DLBCL患者队列中观察到，既往使用特定广谱抗生素与较差的抗CD19 CAR-T生存结果相关。随后，在发现亚组（n=67）和外部验证队列（n=58）中，证实这些抗生素导致显著的肠道和血液代谢组改变，包括短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）和其他阴离子代谢物的变化。此外，通过免疫健全的小鼠模型复现了美罗培南诱导的系统性代谢紊乱及CAR-T疗效下降，并进一步证明SCFAs能增强CAR-T细胞的代谢适应性和肿瘤杀伤能力。

source_materials.title: Antibiotic-induced loss of gut microbiome metabolic output correlates with clinical responses to CAR T-cell therapy.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 区分肿瘤内微生物与肠道微生物的概念和来源，避免混淆两者在免疫治疗中的作用路径。
broader_review_uses.material: 引言部分详细讨论了肿瘤内微生物的三种主要来源（黏膜屏障易位、邻近正常组织起源、血液/淋巴转运），并强调其与肠道微生物的区别。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为背景信息，澄清综述中关于“微生物”定义的边界，帮助读者理解为何某些代谢效应可能源于局部而非全身。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供关于肿瘤内微生物代谢组学研究方法学局限性的讨论。
broader_review_uses.material: Methods and Limitations部分指出样本采集污染、低生物量、静态代谢组学无法追踪动态过程、缺乏因果关系证明等问题。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为批判性评价素材，说明当前领域在确立微生物-宿主互作因果关系方面的技术瓶颈，提示后续研究需谨慎解读相关性数据。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提供未来研究方向，如泛癌种代谢组图谱构建、饮食与非抗癌药物对肿瘤内微生物代谢的影响。
broader_review_uses.material: Future perspectives部分提出的八个方向，包括构建全景图谱、比较肠-瘤微生物代谢差异、确定最佳浓度、探索饮食和非抗癌药物（如抗生素、降糖药）的影响。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为综述的展望部分素材，展示该领域的未解问题和潜在干预策略（如通过饮食或药物调节局部代谢）。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅涵盖肿瘤内微生物，不直接回答肠道微生物如何通过全身循环影响ICIs的问题；部分证据来自动物模型，临床普遍性需结合其他文献验证。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肿瘤内微生物代谢物增强免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效的具体实例和机制。例如，工程菌产生的精氨酸、L. johnsonii产生的IPA、F. nucleatum产生的TMAO以及双歧杆菌产生的肌苷均被报道能增强抗PD-1/PD-L1治疗的疗效，通过增加CD8+ T细胞浸润或激活效应T细胞实现。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答ICIs疗效受微生物代谢影响的机制，特别是当需要区分肠道与肿瘤内来源时，此材料提供了肿瘤内局部的代谢干预证据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制描述多为作者汇总的现有研究结论，需注意不同研究中可能存在相反结果（如TMAO在不同癌症中的作用差异）；部分机制（如其他氨基酸的作用）尚不完全清楚。
facet_contributions.contribution: 详细阐述了特定代谢物调节免疫细胞功能的分子机制。包括：乳酸通过GPCR诱导M2极化和抑制IFN-γ；SCFAs通过GPR109A抑制AKT/mTOR通路；色氨酸衍生物激活AhR受体；胆汁酸调节NF-κB通路等。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释微生物代谢物介导免疫调节的具体信号通路和细胞靶点，丰富对“机制”层面的理解。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述专门聚焦于“肿瘤内”微生物（intratumoural microbes）而非肠道微生物，这与用户关注的“肠道微生物群”有明确界限，但在机制层面（如代谢物对ICIs的影响）提供了重要的对比和补充素材。它详细列举了多种由肿瘤内微生物产生的代谢物（如乳酸、SCFAs、TMAO、肌苷等）如何直接调节免疫细胞功能并增强免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的疗效，可作为解释“非肠道来源的微生物代谢机制”或“局部微环境代谢调控”的重要参考。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 本文核心对象是“肿瘤内微生物”，而非用户主要关注的“肠道微生物群”。虽然机制有重叠，但来源和局部效应不同，不可直接将肿瘤内微生物的发现外推至肠道微生物。
文中提到的许多机制（如精氨酸、TMAO的作用）基于动物模型或体外实验，临床转化存在不确定性，且不同癌症类型中同一代谢物的作用可能相反（如TMAO在乳腺癌中抗肿瘤，在肝癌/结直肠癌中促肿瘤）。
作者声称的“增强免疫治疗疗效”多为预临床证据，临床有效性和最佳浓度尚未确定，需注明这是潜在策略而非既定事实。
topic_handles: Intratumoural microbiota vs Gut microbiota distinction
Metabolite-mediated immune modulation (Lactate, SCFAs, Bile acids, Tryptophan derivatives)
Mechanisms of metabolic reprogramming in TME

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇综述，本研究通过文献检索（PubMed，1980-2025年）收集关于肿瘤内微生物代谢及其对肿瘤微环境和免疫治疗影响的英文文献。采用主题分类法，将代谢物按生化类别（葡萄糖、氨基酸、脂质及其他）进行归纳，分别论述其来源、靶点（如受体、信号通路）、对特定免疫细胞（如CD8+ T细胞、巨噬细胞）的功能影响以及对肿瘤进展的作用。同时，单独章节分析代谢物与不同治疗手段（化疗、放疗、免疫检查点阻断）的相互作用，并在讨论部分总结现有研究的局限性（如因果关系未明、空间异质性忽略等）。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了肿瘤内微生物代谢物分类作用的系统性框架，明确了不同代谢物（乳酸、SCFAs、胆汁酸等）对免疫细胞的具体调节机制及其与免疫检查点抑制剂的协同潜力。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 作为综述，依赖已发表文献，未能提供新的实验数据；所引用的因果证据多来自动物模型或体外实验，临床转化存在物种差异和方法学挑战（如污染、低生物量）；未解决代谢物浓度的最佳阈值问题。

key_findings.conditions: 厌氧菌产生的乳酸
key_findings.finding: 促进肿瘤进展：诱导M2型巨噬细胞极化，抑制CD8+ T细胞和NK细胞的IFN-γ产生，并促进血管生成；与酸性微环境形成自我强化的正反馈循环。

key_findings.conditions: 色氨酸代谢产物（如IPA、吲哚-3-甲醛）
key_findings.finding: 增强抗肿瘤免疫：激活CD8+ T细胞上的AhR受体，促进IFN-γ产生，增强抗PD-1免疫疗法的效果；而犬尿氨酸途径则促进调节性T细胞生成，抑制免疫。

key_findings.conditions: 工程化大肠杆菌产生的精氨酸
key_findings.finding: 增强免疫治疗：增加肿瘤浸润T细胞数量，提高PD-L1阻断抗体的疗效；但高浓度精氨酸也可能通过调节代谢促进肿瘤形成，具有双向效应。

key_findings.conditions: 短链脂肪酸（SCFAs，如丁酸、丙酸）
key_findings.finding: 主要抑制肿瘤：通过GPR109A等受体抑制AKT/mTOR通路诱导癌细胞凋亡，调节细胞因子分泌（如IL-17, IFN-γ），并作为碳源支持免疫细胞活性；效果具有浓度依赖性。

key_findings.conditions: 胆汁酸代谢物（如TUDCA）
key_findings.finding: 复杂调控：在某些癌症中（如HCC），TUDCA可抑制炎症反应并促进CD8+ T细胞浸润，增强PD-1抗体疗效；总体低胆汁酸水平可能与更好的预后相关。

key_findings.conditions: TMAO和肌苷
key_findings.finding: 增强免疫：TMAO通过I型干扰素信号通路激活效应T细胞和M1型巨噬细胞；肌苷通过与A2A受体相互作用增强抗肿瘤T细胞活性，改善免疫治疗疗效。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 阐明肿瘤内微生物代谢物在塑造肿瘤微环境和调节抗肿瘤免疫中的具体作用机制，以及它们如何影响癌症免疫治疗的临床疗效，旨在为基于微生物组的个性化癌症治疗策略提供理论依据。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 肿瘤微环境（TME）内的微生物群及其代谢产物，重点在于这些代谢物如何调节抗肿瘤免疫反应及影响癌症免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂）的疗效。研究对象为肿瘤组织内定植的微生物（intratumoural microbes），区别于肠道微生物群。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本文是一篇综述，系统评估了肿瘤内微生物代谢物对肿瘤微环境和癌症免疫治疗的影响。文章首先区分了肿瘤内微生物与肠道微生物的来源差异，随后分类详细阐述了葡萄糖代谢产物（如乳酸）、氨基酸及其衍生物（如色氨酸、精氨酸）、脂质代谢产物（如短链脂肪酸、胆汁酸）以及其他代谢物（如TMAO、肌苷）在调节免疫细胞功能、细胞因子分泌和肿瘤生长中的具体机制。最后，文章探讨了这些代谢物与化疗、放疗及免疫检查点抑制剂的协同或拮抗作用，并指出了当前研究的方法学局限及未来建立泛癌种代谢组图谱、确定最佳浓度等方向。

source_materials.title: The metabolic dialogue between intratumoural microbes and cancer: implications for immunotherapy

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Discusses the limitations of current microbiome research, including methodological heterogeneity, lack of standardized protocols, and the gap between preclinical findings and clinical translation.
broader_review_uses.material: Critiques the reliance on single-taxa abundance, advocates for topology-based approaches, and highlights logistical barriers like metagenomic turnaround times for precision nutrition.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Provides background on the challenges and future directions in the field, useful for discussing the current state of evidence and areas needing further research.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Summarizes various microbiome-based interventions, including FMT, probiotics, postbiotics, and dietary fiber, detailing their potential benefits and risks.
broader_review_uses.material: Describes FMT from responders vs. healthy donors, encapsulation technologies for probiotics, and the double-edged nature of antibiotic preconditioning and high-fiber diets.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Offers examples of clinical interventions and their outcomes, useful for comparing different strategies to modulate the microbiome for improved ICI outcomes.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Findings are based on a synthesis of various studies with differing methodologies; causal relationships are often inferred from preclinical models or observational data rather than definitive clinical trials.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details the context-dependent nature of microbiome-ICI interactions, showing that beneficial taxa vary by cancer type and ICI regimen (e.g., Bacteroides for CTLA-4, Faecalibacterium for PD-1, variable role of Akk). It also discusses the trade-off between efficacy and toxicity, noting that some microbes protective in one context may be detrimental in another.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to explain why microbiome signatures are not universal and depend on specific treatment protocols and patient populations. Helps address questions about heterogeneity in ICI response.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Many mechanisms are described from murine models or in vitro studies; human concentration thresholds and spatial dynamics within the tumor microenvironment are noted as undefined.
facet_contributions.contribution: Provides specific molecular mechanisms linking microbes/metabolites to immune modulation. For example, it describes how LGG and BF839 activate the cGAS-STING pathway, how tryptophan metabolites act via AhR, and how SCFAs influence T-cell function and barrier integrity through epigenetic and receptor-mediated pathways.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Offers detailed mechanistic explanations for how gut microbes influence ICI efficacy and toxicity, suitable for sections discussing biological pathways and molecular targets.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review offers a structured framework for understanding the 'gut-metabolite-immune' axis in the context of solid tumor immunotherapy. It provides detailed mechanistic insights into how specific microbial taxa and metabolites modulate ICI efficacy and toxicity, serving as a valuable resource for explaining biological mechanisms and contextualizing clinical heterogeneity. It also summarizes the current state of microbiome-based interventions, highlighting both promising strategies and translational barriers.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative synthesis and does not provide quantitative meta-analytic results; effect sizes and statistical significance should not be inferred from this text alone.
Many mechanistic insights are derived from preclinical models (mice) or small clinical cohorts; extrapolation to broader human populations requires caution.
The role of specific microbes (e.g., Akkermansia) can be context-dependent and even contradictory across studies; avoid treating any single taxon as universally beneficial or detrimental.
Claims about the efficacy of interventions like FMT or probiotics are primarily based on early-phase trials or preclinical data; robust clinical validation is still needed.
topic_handles: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs): PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4, LAG-3, TIGIT, TIM-3
Gut Microbiota Taxa: Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila, Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcaceae
Microbial Metabolites: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), Tryptophan derivatives (3-IAld, IPA, ILA), TMAO, Inosine, Secondary bile acids, Polyamines
Signaling Pathways: cGAS-STING, NOD2, AhR, PPARa, HDAC, PERK-GSDME
Interventions: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT), Probiotics (LGG, BF839), Postbiotics, Dietary Fiber
Clinical Outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), Immune-related Adverse Events (irAEs)

study_summary_A.approach: The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Embase up to May 1, 2026. They included original studies, RCTs, cohort studies, and preclinical investigations examining the effects of gut microbiota or metabolites on ICI efficacy or toxicities. Data extraction was guided by STORMS guidelines. As a narrative review, formal risk-of-bias assessment, quality grading, and statistical meta-analysis were not performed. The synthesis is organized thematically: first covering ICI mechanisms, then the heterogeneity of microbiome-ICI interactions, followed by specific metabolite classes, clinical heterogeneity of irAEs, and finally microbiome-based interventions.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive mechanistic synthesis linking specific gut microbes and metabolites to ICI efficacy and irAE mitigation, categorizing interventions by their molecular targets (STING, NOD2, AhR, etc.).
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a narrative review, it lacks formal risk-of-bias assessment and statistical meta-analysis. Findings are largely derived from preclinical models or small clinical cohorts with limited covariate adjustment. The review acknowledges significant methodological heterogeneity across studies and notes that many proposed biomarkers and interventions require validation in large-scale, standardized longitudinal studies.

key_findings.conditions: Melanoma patients treated with anti-CTLA-4 (ipilimumab)
key_findings.finding: CTLA-4 blockade reshapes the microbiota, favoring Bacteroides species (e.g., B. fragilis, B. thetaiotaomicron), which are critical for antitumor efficacy.

key_findings.conditions: NSCLC patients treated with anti-PD-1
key_findings.finding: High relative abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk-high) was associated with worse overall survival compared to Akk-low groups, challenging the binary 'good vs bad' bacteria concept and highlighting cohort/cancer-type dependency.

key_findings.conditions: Various ICI regimens
key_findings.finding: Microbial influence is context-dependent; different ICIs rely on distinct microbial signatures (e.g., Faecalibacterium/Ruminococcaceae for anti-PD-1 vs. Bacteroides for anti-CTLA-4).

key_findings.conditions: Tryptophan metabolites (3-IAld, IPA)
key_findings.finding: 3-IAld alleviates colitis and enhances efficacy via AhR/IL-22; IPA provides cardioprotection via AhR/PI3K/AKT signaling.

key_findings.conditions: SCFAs (Butyrate, Propionate, Acetate)
key_findings.finding: Butyrate protects against cardiotoxicity via PPARa-CYP4X1 and enhances antigen presentation via HDAC inhibition; Propionate/Acetate promote Treg homeostasis and memory CD8+ T-cell differentiation.

key_findings.conditions: TMAO
key_findings.finding: Triggers immunogenic tumor cell death (pyroptosis) via PERK-GSDME pathway, recruiting CD8+ T cells.

key_findings.conditions: Probiotics (LGG, BF839, Akk)
key_findings.finding: LGG and BF839 activate cGAS-STING axis in dendritic cells to enhance CD8+ T cell infiltration; Akk produces c-di-AMP which directly activates STING.

key_findings.conditions: FMT interventions
key_findings.finding: FMT from long-term responders to PD-1 therapy showed higher efficacy than healthy donors; response correlated with loss of deleterious baseline species rather than just engraftment of donor strains.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: The clinical utility of ICIs is limited by interpatient variability in efficacy and the occurrence of systemic toxicities (irAEs). The review aims to systematically delineate the microbiome-metabolite-immune axis to understand these variations and optimize the balance between therapeutic gain and toxicity, ultimately guiding the development of precise microbial interventions.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The review focuses on the gut microbiome and its metabolic byproducts as systemic regulators of immune function, specifically in the context of cancer immunotherapy using immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). It covers mechanisms of ICI action (PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4, LAG-3, TIGIT, TIM-3), the heterogeneity of microbiome-ICI interactions across different cancer types and cohorts, microbial metabolites (tryptophan derivatives, SCFAs, TMAO, inosine, bile acids, polyamines) as mediators of efficacy and toxicity, and microbiome-based interventions including probiotics, FMT, postbiotics, and dietary fiber.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on how the gut microbiota and microbe-derived metabolites regulate the efficacy and immune-related adverse events (irAEs) of ICIs. It highlights specific taxa like Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, and Akkermansia muciniphila that potentiate therapeutic responses via pathways such as cGAS-STING and NOD2. The review also details how microbial metabolites protect organs like the heart and colon from inflammation while enhancing anti-tumor immunity. It evaluates emerging interventions like FMT and next-generation probiotics, noting that while preclinical and Phase I trials show feasibility, substantial hurdles remain regarding cohort heterogeneity, methodological standardization, and the need for large-scale longitudinal studies to establish reproducible predictive models.

source_materials.title: Navigating the gut–metabolite–immune axis: enhancing efficacy and mitigating toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 帮助综述界定研究范围的演变，强调将微生物-免疫互作研究从黑色素瘤扩展到其他实体瘤的必要性。
broader_review_uses.material: 指出既往研究主要集中在黑色素瘤，而NMSC数据有限。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 背景与领域扩展

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 为综述中评估不同研究设计的优缺点提供实例，特别是如何整合多组学数据以增强对微生物-宿主互作的理解。
broader_review_uses.material: 展示了结合纵向16S测序、功能预测（PICRUSt2）和非靶向代谢组学的综合分析方法。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 方法论参考

facet_contributions.boundaries: 样本量小，仅具探索性；部分菌属在不同个体间不一致，提示功能冗余而非单一物种决定论。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了NMSC患者中区分ICI响应者与非响应者的具体微生物属/种列表（如Bilophila wadsworthia在NR中高丰度），以及跨肿瘤类型的通用差异菌属。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于综述中列举不同实体瘤类型中特异性微生物标志物的差异，支持“微生物标志物具有肿瘤类型依赖性”的观点。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 基于预测（PICRUSt2）和小样本实测代谢组学；作者承认这些观察需要更大规模的目标代谢组学验证；不能直接推断因果机制。
facet_contributions.contribution: 揭示了NMSC中微生物代谢功能的复杂性：预测显示SCFA产生通路在非响应者中富集，且检测到NR中L-精氨酸水平较高，这与“SCFA促进免疫反应”和“高L-精氨酸改善预后”的常见假设相悖。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于综述中讨论微生物代谢产物对ICI疗效影响的争议性或情境依赖性机制，特别是作为反例或需要更细致解析的案例，说明简单的相关性不足以解释复杂的免疫微环境交互。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文为非黑色素瘤皮肤癌（NMSC）这一特定实体瘤亚型提供了肠道微生物群与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）疗效关联的初步实证数据。其核心价值在于揭示了不同于黑色素瘤研究的潜在微生物-代谢特征，特别是关于短链脂肪酸（SCFA）和L-精氨酸的意外发现，为综述中讨论“不同肿瘤类型中微生物机制的特异性”及“微生物代谢物对免疫治疗的调节作用”提供了具体的反面案例或复杂情境素材。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该研究为探索性小规模研究，结果不可外推为临床诊断标准。
发现的代谢物差异（如SCFA和L-精氨酸）方向与部分既往文献相反，需谨慎解读，避免将其视为确凿的否定证据，而应视为提示机制复杂性的线索。
α多样性无显著变化，表明在ICI治疗期间，NMSC患者的微生物群落整体丰富度可能保持稳定，差异主要体现在特定类群和代谢功能上。
topic_handles: 免疫检查点抑制剂 (ICI) 疗效预测
肠道微生物群落结构 (16S rRNA)

study_summary_A.approach: 采用纵向队列设计，收集NMSC患者在ICI治疗前、中、后的粪便样本。使用16S rRNA V1-V2扩增子测序进行微生物分类学分析，利用LEfSe识别差异丰度菌属/种，PICRUSt2预测功能通路。同时，对部分CSCC样本进行非靶向代谢组学分析，通过KEGG数据库进行代谢通路富集分析。临床反应依据RECIST v.1.1标准定义为完全/部分缓解（R）或疾病进展（NR）。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了首个关于NMSC患者肠道微生物群与ICI反应关联的探索性证据，确定了潜在的差异菌群标志物和代谢通路，为后续大规模验证研究奠定了基础。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 样本量极小（总n=21，CSCC仅n=11，代谢组学仅n=6），结果可能受个体异质性影响；未观察到α多样性的显著变化；部分发现（如SCFA和L-精氨酸的作用）与既往假设或研究矛盾，需进一步验证；仅为相关性观察，无法确立因果关系。

key_findings.conditions: 所有肿瘤类型（BCC, MCC, CSCC）合并分析
key_findings.finding: 发现10个在响应者（R）和非响应者（NR）之间具有显著差异的细菌属；PCoA显示不同临床反应组之间存在分离趋势。

key_findings.conditions: 皮肤鳞状细胞癌（CSCC）亚组分析
key_findings.finding: 识别出10个差异属和20个差异种。预测的功能通路分析显示，短链脂肪酸（SCFA）产生通路在NR中富集，而12条其他通路在R中富集。

key_findings.conditions: CSCC患者粪便代谢组学分析
key_findings.finding: 鉴定出9个与ICI疗效相关的KEGG代谢通路。L-精氨酸浓度在NR中较高（与既往癌症研究中高L-精氨酸预示良好预后的发现相反）；甾体激素（如孕酮）在R中浓度较高。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 在缺乏针对NMSC患者的数据背景下，肠道微生物群的结构和功能特征是否与NMSC患者对ICI治疗的临床反应（响应vs非响应）相关联？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 非黑色素瘤皮肤癌（NMSC）患者，包括基底细胞癌（BCC, n=5）、默克尔细胞癌（MCC, n=5）和皮肤鳞状细胞癌（CSCC, n=11）。研究对象为接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的21名个体，共收集68份纵向粪便样本。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本研究是一项探索性研究，旨在调查肠道微生物群的结构和功能特征与非黑色素瘤皮肤癌（NMSC）患者对免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗反应的关联。鉴于既往研究多集中于黑色素瘤，该研究填补了NMSC领域的数据空白。作者通过16S rRNA V1-V2基因扩增子测序分析细菌组成，并结合非靶向代谢组学检测粪便代谢物，比较了ICI治疗响应者（R）与非响应者（NR）之间的差异。研究发现，尽管α多样性随时间无显著变化，但在属和种水平上存在显著的菌群差异，且特定代谢通路和代谢物与治疗效果相关。

source_materials.title: Gut microbiome features associate with immune checkpoint inhibitor response in individuals with non-melanoma skin cancers: an exploratory study

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 帮助综述建立微生物组在肿瘤微环境中整体角色的理论背景，超越单一的基因突变视角
broader_review_uses.material: 将肿瘤视为包含“肿瘤内微生物群”的复杂生态系统，强调微生物是癌症生物学中动态且情境依赖的调节层
broader_review_uses.purpose: 提供领域背景与概念框架

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提醒在总结肠道微生物群益处时，需注意其潜在的负面效应和肿瘤特异性限制，避免过度概括
broader_review_uses.material: 指出微生物调节活动高度依赖于肿瘤类型和情境（context dependent and tumor type specific），且某些干预可能导致耐受性和毒性
broader_review_uses.purpose: 列举反例或复杂性以平衡综述观点

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 为综述讨论当前研究的局限性和未来临床转化路径提供参考依据
broader_review_uses.material: 建议将微生物组元素逐步纳入标准护理评估模板，以实现多层次个体变异评估；强调需要进一步的机制和临床验证
broader_review_uses.purpose: 提供未来研究方向与方法学启示

facet_contributions.boundaries: 证据主要来自临床前模型（preclinical models）和部分观察性关联，需注明其外推到人类临床的局限性；不同肿瘤类型的结果不能混为一谈，需强调情境依赖性。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群影响实体瘤ICI疗效的具体实例和关联证据：1) 肠道链球菌富集与肿瘤内CD8+ T细胞浸润正相关，且FMT可挽救抗PD-1反应；2) SCFAs在NSCLC等肿瘤中作为化疗-免疫治疗效力的介质；3) 不同肿瘤类型（黑色素瘤、PDAC）对微生物干预的反应存在异质性。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于支持肠道微生物群对ICI疗效具有正向调节作用的论点，并提供具体的菌群-效应分子对应关系作为证据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制细节多来自动物模型或体外研究（如PDAC模型中的TMAO实验），作者明确指出这些介导物的全身代谢影响和安全谱系尚待研究，不能直接等同于人体内的确切机制。
facet_contributions.contribution: 详细阐述了介导效应的机制路径：1) 免疫调节：微生物信号促进CD8+/Tc1程序，刺激细胞毒性反应；2) 代谢重编程：色氨酸分解代谢和短链代谢物介导的信号改变效应T细胞状态；3) 特定代谢物作用：TMAO在PDAC中与ICI联用增强疗效；4) 局部与全身联系：肠道微生物通过代谢物影响全身免疫基调，肿瘤内微生物维持局部炎症回路。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释肠道微生物群影响ICI疗效的具体生物学机制，特别是代谢物和免疫细胞状态的交互作用。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何通过代谢产物和免疫调节影响实体瘤免疫治疗提供了重要的机制背景和策略分类。它直接关联F1（肠道微生物如何调节ICI疗效）和F2（介导机制），特别是通过具体案例（如链球菌、SCFAs、TMAO）展示了跨器官（肠道-肿瘤）的互作模式，并区分了不同肿瘤类型的特异性反应。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述主要基于摘要和片段，具体机制（如TMAO的作用）明确标注为在PDAC模型中的发现，不可直接推广至所有实体瘤
作者提到的“改善ICI疗效”主要基于临床前模型（preclinical models），需区分动物实验结果与人类临床证据
文中提到的“微生物组定义的治疗”仍处于新兴阶段，强调需要进一步验证，不应视为已确立的标准疗法
不同肿瘤类型（黑色素瘤、PDAC、NSCLC）的结果具有特异性，跨肿瘤类型的比较需谨慎，避免混淆机制
topic_handles: 肠道微生物群与肿瘤内免疫细胞的关联（如链球菌与CD8+ T细胞）
微生物代谢物介导的免疫调节（SCFAs, TMAO, 色氨酸代谢）
免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）响应的情境依赖性（黑色素瘤 vs PDAC vs NSCLC）
微生物组靶向治疗策略（FMT, 工程化OMVs, 代谢物补充）
肿瘤微环境中的局部生态位与全身免疫稳态的连接

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇综述，本文通过梳理近期在高通量测序、空间组学和整合多组学分析方面的进展，构建“肿瘤作为复杂生态系统”的概念。作者综合了关于微生物与免疫系统、免疫代谢重编程、慢性炎症及基因组不稳定性的相互作用文献，归纳出免疫调节、代谢重编程和信号重组等机制，并评估了从生物标志物到工程化微生物外膜囊泡（OMVs）等新兴治疗策略的证据等级和临床场景。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了肿瘤内微生物群在癌症生物学中作为动态且情境依赖的调节层的集成框架，涵盖了从基础机制（免疫、代谢、信号）到临床应用（生物标志物、治疗策略）的多层级内容
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索策略、纳入排除标准及数据提取方法；结论主要基于作者对现有研究的综合，部分机制（如特定代谢物的安全性）仍需进一步验证

key_findings.conditions: 黑色素瘤及其他模型中，微生物信号通过色氨酸分解代谢和短链代谢物介导的信号传导
key_findings.finding: 作者指出这些信号似乎能重编程效应T细胞状态并增加抗肿瘤免疫力，从而在临床前模型中提高免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）的疗效

key_findings.conditions: 胰腺导管腺癌（PDAC）模型中，肠道来源代谢物氧化三甲胺（TMAO）与抗PD-1和/或抗Tim3联合使用
key_findings.finding: 结果显示肿瘤负荷减少，生存期优于单药治疗

key_findings.conditions: 肠道微生物群变化与效应免疫功能的配对
key_findings.finding: 肠道链球菌（Streptococcus）富集与肿瘤内GrzB+细胞和CD8+ T细胞浸润增加相关；抗PD-1治疗的活性反应可通过粪菌移植（FMT）或靶向定植挽救

key_findings.conditions: 非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）及其他肿瘤中的化疗-免疫治疗
key_findings.finding: 微生物衍生的短链脂肪酸（SCFAs） emerging as mediators of efficacy，连接免疫细胞状态和微环境稳态，作为增强治疗反应的潜在靶点

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管高通量测序等技术已证实肿瘤中存在可重复检测的微生物群落，但现有证据仍零散且多为描述性，缺乏对微生物组成、功能机制及临床转化应用的系统整合，特别是在不同肿瘤类型和微环境背景下的差异。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 肿瘤组织内的微生物群（intratumoral microbiota）及其在癌症生物学中的作用，重点涉及免疫治疗响应、代谢重编程及微环境调控。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 该综述旨在解决当前关于肿瘤内微生物的证据碎片化、描述性为主且缺乏系统性整合的问题。文章总结了微生物多样性、肿瘤类型特异性关联以及多层级机制（包括免疫调节、代谢重编程和信号通路重塑），并讨论了其在生物标志物发现、预后分层和微生物组靶向治疗中的应用。特别关注肿瘤微环境、微生物衍生的代谢物以及免疫治疗反应的决定因素，提出将微生物组纳入精准肿瘤学框架的集成方案。

source_materials.title: Intratumoral Microorganisms in Tumors: Current Understanding and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 背景与争议梳理
broader_review_uses.material: 文中提到的既往meta分析结果矛盾（Li et al., Qin et al., Liu et al.），以及本研究通过扩大样本量和纳入会议摘要来解决这些矛盾的努力。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述的背景部分，说明该领域研究现状的复杂性和本综述纳入此类大样本荟萃分析的必要性。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 临床实践指导意义
broader_review_uses.material: 建议对于接受ICI治疗的患者，应严格控制PPI的使用，特别是在ICI开始前；若必须使用，短期伴随使用似乎不影响生存。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 用于综述的讨论或结论部分，探讨干预措施的可能性。即通过管理共病用药（如PPI）来优化ICI疗效的策略。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅证明统计学关联，不直接展示菌群变化过程。不能直接用于解释分子机制，只能作为现象描述的证据。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了PPI使用对ICI疗效影响的定量汇总证据：整体HR>1，但在不同癌症类型（NSCLC/UC vs. RCC/Melanoma）和使用时窗上存在显著差异。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道菌群如何调节ICI疗效”中的外部因素干扰部分。特别是用于说明当肠道菌群受到药物（PPI）干扰时，ICI疗效可能受损，但这种影响并非在所有情境下都一致。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制解释主要依赖作者对既往文献的引用和推测，而非本研究的实证数据。需结合其他提供直接微生物组数据的研究共同构建机制图景。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提出了“使用时窗”作为潜在机制的解释线索：仅在ICI前长期使用PPI才导致疗效下降，暗示需要时间累积的菌群失调（如细菌丰富度降低）是中介因素。同时指出特定菌属（Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruminococcus sp.）可能在NSCLC中起关键作用，而PPI对其有负面影响。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于辅助回答“机制是什么”。虽然本文未提供直接机制数据，但其讨论部分引用的文献和观察到的时窗效应，为“菌群组成改变->免疫微环境改变->疗效下降”这一链条提供了临床层面的合理性支持和边界条件。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文为综述提供了关键的宏观流行病学证据，证实了PPI使用与ICI疗效之间的负面关联，并提出了“使用时窗”这一重要调节变量。它有助于解释为何不同研究间存在异质性，并为“肠道菌群介导”假说提供了间接的临床支持线索（即长期菌群扰动才有害）。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该研究为观察性数据的荟萃分析，存在混杂因素风险（尽管进行了多变量调整，但仍可能有未测量混杂）。
“无显著影响”不等于“无关联”，特别是在RCC和黑色素瘤亚组中，可能受限于统计效能或生物学特异性。
使用时窗的分类（基线、前60天、同期）是基于原始研究报告的聚合，不同研究的具体定义可能存在细微差异，需谨慎外推。
作者提出的机制解释（如特定菌属）是基于文献回顾和自身结果的推断，并非本研究直接测得，阅读时需区分事实发现与理论假设。

study_summary_A.approach: 采用PRISMA 2020指南进行系统综述和荟萃分析。检索EMBASE、MEDLINE/PubMed、Cochrane Library及主要肿瘤学会议摘要。纳入标准包括报告ICI治疗癌症患者中PPI使用者与非使用者的OS或PFS HR值的研究。数据提取后，使用随机效应模型合并HR，并通过Cochran's Q检验和I²指数评估异质性。进一步按PPI使用时窗、癌症类型、ICI类型、治疗线数和地理区域进行亚组分析，并使用Meta回归和Egger's检验评估偏倚。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了目前最大规模的证据综合，确认了PPI使用与ICI疗效降低之间的整体负相关关系，并细化了这种关联依赖于PPI使用时窗（长期/预防性 vs. 短期/伴随）和癌症类型。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给材料未交代具体的微生物组测序数据或机制验证实验，结论基于流行病学观察数据的汇总。亚组分析受限于原始研究中缺失的临床细节（如具体PPI种类、饮食、种族、PD-L1状态），且部分亚组（如抗CTLA-4）样本量不足，无法得出确切结论。

key_findings.conditions: 总体人群（33项研究，约15,957名OS患者）
PPI使用时窗：基线治疗或ICI前60天内开始
key_findings.finding: 在基线使用PPI（Group A）或ICI前60天内开始使用PPI（Group B）的患者中，OS和PFS均显著缩短；而在ICI治疗期间或之后才开始使用PPI（Group C）时，未观察到显著的生存负面影响。

key_findings.conditions: 癌症类型：非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和尿路上皮癌（UC）
key_findings.finding: PPI使用显著缩短NSCLC和UC患者的OS和PFS；而在肾细胞癌（RCC）和黑色素瘤患者中，未观察到显著的生存影响。

key_findings.conditions: ICI类型：抗PD-1/PD-L1单抗
key_findings.finding: 在抗PD-1、抗PD-L1及抗PD-(L)1治疗亚组中，PPI使用显著降低生存率；由于样本量极少，抗CTLA-4单药或联合疗法的亚组结果不具统计效力。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管已有研究表明肠道菌群调节可能影响ICI疗效，且PPI已知会改变肠道菌群，但既往关于PPI与ICI联用对患者生存结局影响的观察结果存在矛盾。本研究旨在通过整合现有证据，明确PPI使用是否以及如何在不同临床情境下影响ICI治疗的生存获益。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的实体瘤患者，考察质子泵抑制剂（PPI）的使用与总生存期（OS）和无进展生存期（PFS）之间的关联。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 这是一篇系统综述和荟萃分析，旨在解决关于PPI使用对ICI疗效影响的研究结果矛盾问题。作者检索了截至2022年3月的多项数据库及会议摘要，纳入比较ICI单药与ICI联合PPI治疗患者的生存数据研究。通过随机效应模型汇总风险比（HR），并进行亚组分析和Meta回归，以探索异质性来源并确定特定人群中的关联模式。

source_materials.title: Association of proton pump inhibitor use with survival outcomes in cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Discusses the impact of diet (high fiber, ketogenic, fasting) on cancer treatment outcomes and microbiome composition.
broader_review_uses.material: Summarizes studies showing high-fiber diets improve ICI response, ketogenic diets enhance chemo/radiation efficacy, and fasting mimicking diets show promise in breast cancer. Mentions ongoing trials.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Provides background on non-microbial interventions (diet) that interact with the microbiome and affect treatment outcomes. Useful for discussing holistic approaches or confounding factors related to lifestyle.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Addresses the negative impact of antibiotic use on cancer treatment efficacy, particularly ICIs.
broader_review_uses.material: Reviews clinical studies showing reduced PFS/OS in patients receiving antibiotics before ICI, linked to microbiome disruption.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Highlights a critical confounding factor (antibiotic exposure) that can negatively impact ICI efficacy. Important for considering patient history and treatment protocols.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Explores the role of the microbiome in treatment-related toxicity (irAEs, GVHD).
broader_review_uses.material: Links specific microbial taxa to the development of irAEs and GVHD, suggesting potential for microbiome-based mitigation strategies.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Provides context on the dual role of the microbiome in both efficacy and toxicity, which is relevant for understanding the overall impact of microbiome modulation.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Most evidence is observational; causality is not established. Some findings are from small cohorts or single centers. Conflicting results exist for certain taxa (e.g., A. muciniphila).
facet_contributions.contribution: Summarizes clinical evidence linking specific gut microbial signatures (e.g., Ruminococcaceae, Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila) to improved response rates to ICIs in solid tumors like melanoma, NSCLC, and RCC. Also notes conflicting data regarding A. muciniphila abundance.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to support the claim that specific gut microbiome compositions are associated with enhanced efficacy of ICIs in solid tumors. Provides examples of microbial taxa to consider as potential biomarkers.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Many mechanistic details are derived from preclinical mouse models. Human validation of specific metabolic pathways is limited. The review acknowledges heterogeneity and complexity in these mechanisms.
facet_contributions.contribution: Describes proposed mechanisms for microbiome-mediated modulation of ICI efficacy, including metabolite production (inosine, SCFAs) influencing T-cell activation, and the role of commensal bacteria in systemic immune priming. Also discusses how antibiotics disrupt these mechanisms.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Provides mechanistic hypotheses for how the gut microbiome affects ICI response, such as through metabolite signaling and immune cell modulation. Highlights the detrimental effect of antibiotics on these pathways.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review provides a broad synthesis of how the gut microbiome and diet influence the efficacy and toxicity of cancer treatments, particularly immunotherapy. It offers valuable context on specific microbial signatures associated with response/resistance to ICIs, the negative impact of antibiotics, and the potential of dietary interventions (fiber, ketogenic) and FMT. This material is useful for establishing the background of microbiome-treatment interactions, identifying key microbial targets, and understanding the current state of translational research in this field.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative summary, not a systematic review or meta-analysis. Findings should be interpreted as indicative trends rather than definitive conclusions.
Many associations are correlative; causal relationships are often inferred from preclinical models and require further validation in controlled human trials.
Conflicting results exist for certain microbial taxa (e.g., Akkermansia muciniphila), highlighting the complexity and context-dependency of microbiome-treatment interactions.
Clinical trial data cited are often preliminary or from small cohorts; long-term efficacy and safety of microbiome-based interventions remain to be fully established.

study_summary_A.approach: The authors conducted a narrative review of existing literature, including clinical cohorts, preclinical models, and ongoing clinical trials. They synthesized findings on microbial associations with treatment response/resistance across different cancer types and modalities. The review also evaluated the mechanistic insights from preclinical studies and summarized the results of dietary intervention trials and FMT studies. No systematic search strategy is described in the provided text.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive summary of the association between gut microbiome composition and response/toxicity to various cancer treatments, highlighting key microbial taxa and dietary factors.
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a narrative review, it does not present new primary data or a systematic meta-analysis. Many findings are based on observational studies or small clinical trials, and causal mechanisms are often inferred from preclinical models rather than confirmed in large-scale human studies.

key_findings.conditions: Immunotherapy (ICI) in melanoma, NSCLC, RCC
key_findings.finding: Specific gut microbial taxa (e.g., Ruminococcaceae, Bifidobacteriaceae, Akkermansia muciniphila) are associated with improved response to ICIs. However, overabundance of A. muciniphila may be linked to poorer outcomes in some contexts.

key_findings.conditions: Chemotherapy (gemcitabine, cyclophosphamide)
key_findings.finding: Gut microbes can either undermine chemotherapy efficacy (e.g., via bacterial enzymes modifying drug activity) or enhance it (e.g., by promoting immune priming through translocation of specific bacteria).

key_findings.conditions: Antibiotic use prior to ICI
key_findings.finding: Broad-spectrum antibiotic use is associated with reduced efficacy of ICIs and worse survival outcomes, likely due to disruption of the gut microbiome.

key_findings.conditions: Dietary interventions (High Fiber, Ketogenic, Fasting)
key_findings.finding: High-fiber diets are associated with improved response to ICIs, potentially mediated by increased microbial diversity and metabolite production. Ketogenic diets and fasting mimicking diets show promise in enhancing chemotherapy/radiation efficacy in preclinical and early clinical settings.

key_findings.conditions: Toxicity (irAEs, GVHD)
key_findings.finding: Specific microbial signatures are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs) and graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Modulation of the microbiome may help mitigate these toxicities.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: To provide an updated overview of the scientific evidence regarding the interaction between gut microbes, diet, and cancer treatment outcomes (response and toxicity), and to identify opportunities for therapeutic modulation of these factors.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The review covers the role of the gut microbiome and diet in cancer treatment response and toxicity, focusing on immunotherapy (ICIs), chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and adoptive cell therapies. It includes clinical cohort studies, preclinical models, and ongoing clinical trials.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This review summarizes current evidence on how the gut microbiome influences the efficacy and toxicity of various cancer treatments, particularly immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). It highlights specific microbial signatures associated with response or resistance to ICIs, chemotherapy, and other therapies. The paper also discusses the impact of dietary interventions (high fiber, ketogenic, fasting) and antibiotic use on treatment outcomes. Finally, it explores strategies for modulating the microbiome, such as fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), probiotics, and prebiotics, to improve patient outcomes and reduce toxicity.

source_materials.title: Monitoring and Modulating Diet and Gut Microbes to Enhance Response and Reduce Toxicity to Cancer Treatment

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 背景与临床实践启示
broader_review_uses.material: 文章指出ABT是肿瘤患者中最常用的药物之一，且存在过度使用现象；建议进行严格的抗生素管理（antibiotic stewardship）。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 作为综述中讨论临床转化意义或未来研究方向的部分素材，强调识别和管理此类可逆宿主因素的重要性。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 对比视角：空间微生物组差异
broader_review_uses.material: 讨论部分引用Riaz等人的研究，指出在某些局部治疗背景下，瘤内细菌而非肠道菌群可能是主要的耐药驱动因素。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 提供 nuanced 的观点，说明微生物组对ICI的影响具有空间和情境依赖性（肠道 vs 瘤内），避免综述将微生物组作用简单化。这有助于界定综述中关于“gut microbiome”特定范围的边界。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅证实了相关性，未直接证明因果机制；主要针对生存终点，不直接回答初始肿瘤缩小（ORR）的情况。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了ABT暴露与ICI疗效（OS/PFS）之间负相关性的最新荟萃分析数据（HR=1.16 for OS）。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于论证宿主因素（特别是药物干预导致的菌群改变）如何具体影响ICI在实体瘤中的临床疗效。可引用其关于NSCLC亚组的一致性结果来增强论点的稳健性。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 这些机制描述基于作者引用的先验知识和文献综述，而非本荟萃分析本身的实验验证；属于理论解释层面，需结合其他提供直接微生物组测序数据的论文共同构建机制链条。
facet_contributions.contribution: 在讨论部分详细阐述了ABT导致菌群失调（减少Akkermansia, Bifidobacterium等有益菌）从而干扰树突状细胞成熟、抗原呈递和CD8+ T细胞 priming 的生物学机制。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释“为什么”抗生素会影响ICI疗效，提供从微生物群到免疫反应的潜在通路解释。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文为综述提供了关于“抗生素使用对ICI疗效负面影响”的最新定量证据汇总。其核心价值在于确认了这一关联在多个实体瘤中的普遍性，并特别指出了NSCLC亚组的稳健性。对于综述而言，它可作为支持“肠道菌群介导的ICI疗效调节”这一主题中负面调节因子的关键实证材料，同时其讨论部分提供的机制解释（如菌群失调导致抗原呈递受损）有助于回答机制相关问题。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该研究为观察性数据的综合，不能确立因果关系，仅表明关联。
结果主要反映的是“系统性”抗生素暴露对“肠道”菌群的影响，不直接代表瘤内微生物组的变化。
异质性中等至较高，合并估计值需谨慎解读，特别是PFS结果未达到统计显著性。
所给材料未提供按抗生素种类（如β-内酰胺类 vs 氟喹诺酮类）细分的具体效应量，仅提及广泛使用的种类，因此在分类比较时需注明数据粒度不足。
topic_handles: Gut dysbiosis mechanism in ICI resistance

study_summary_A.approach: 采用系统综述和荟萃分析方法。检索策略限定于2018-2025年发表的研究，纳入标准为报告了ABT暴露时间窗及生存结局（HR及95% CI）的回顾性或前瞻性临床研究的实体瘤患者。排除动物研究、综述及数据不全者。使用DerSimonian和Laird方法的随机效应模型计算合并HR值，以处理临床和方法学上的异质性。进行敏感性分析（限于NSCLC亚组）以评估结果的稳定性，并通过漏斗图和Egger检验评估发表偏倚。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了2018-2025年间最新的大样本量证据，量化了ABT对ICI疗效的负面影响，特别是强调了近期暴露（靠近ICI启动期）的重要性。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的抗生素类别特异性效应分析结果；由于纳入研究多为回顾性，存在残余混杂因素（如适应症混杂）的风险；无法评估客观缓解率（ORR）等治疗反应指标，仅关注生存终点；未能进行剂量-反应关系分析。

key_findings.conditions: 所有纳入的实体瘤患者（n=52,489），随机效应模型
key_findings.finding: ABT暴露与总生存期（OS）显著恶化相关，风险增加约16%（HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.03-1.29）。

key_findings.conditions: 所有纳入患者，随机效应模型
key_findings.finding: ABT暴露与无进展生存期（PFS）恶化呈趋势性相关，风险增加约11%（HR=1.11, 95% CI 0.95-1.27），但未达到统计学显著性。

key_findings.conditions: 非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）亚组敏感性分析
key_findings.finding: ABT暴露 consistently 与更差的生存结局相关，支持总体结论。

key_findings.conditions: ICI联合化疗亚组
key_findings.finding: ABT暴露与死亡风险增加12%相关（HR=1.12, 95% CI 1.08-1.16），且无显著异质性。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂改善了多种实体瘤的预后，但持久响应率有限。鉴于肠道微生物群在调节抗肿瘤免疫中的作用，全身性抗生素治疗（ABT）是否通过破坏肠道菌群进而损害ICIs的临床疗效？不同肿瘤类型和治疗背景下，这种关联的一致性和 magnitude 如何？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 实体瘤患者接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗期间，全身性抗生素治疗（ABT）暴露对总生存期（OS）和无进展生存期（PFS）的影响。研究涵盖2018年至2025年间发表的观察性临床研究，重点关注肿瘤类型、ICI治疗方案及ABT暴露的时间窗口。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本研究是一项遵循PRISMA 2020指南的系统综述和荟萃分析，旨在评估实体瘤患者在接受ICIs治疗时，全身性抗生素使用对生存结局的影响。通过检索PubMed、Scopus和EMBASE数据库，筛选出15项包含52,489名患者的研究进行定量合成。主要发现显示，在随机效应模型下，ABT暴露与较差的总生存期显著相关（HR=1.16），并与无进展生存期的恶化趋势相关（HR=1.11）。在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）亚组中，这种负面影响得到一致支持。研究认为ABT可能通过诱导肠道菌群失调削弱抗肿瘤免疫反应，从而降低ICIs疗效，并呼吁在ICIs治疗期间谨慎使用抗生素。

source_materials.title: A Silent Saboteur of Immunotherapy: Antibiotic Use and Its Impact on Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Efficacy, a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Recent Studies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 可作为综述中讨论研究设计优化或跨物种转化挑战时的背景参考，强调多尺度研究的重要性。
broader_review_uses.material: 倡导‘平行动物-人类研究’模式，即动物模型指导临床设计，临床观察反馈至动物研究。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 方法论背景

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 帮助构建‘宿主因素-微生物群-免疫治疗’的综合框架，说明为何在研究微生物群时需考虑饮食和运动等能量平衡要素。
broader_review_uses.material: 将能量平衡（饮食、运动、身体成分）视为影响癌症发展和预后的整体宿主因素集合。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 概念框架

facet_contributions.boundaries: 该论文主要提供概念关联和文献综述层面的证据，未提供针对特定固体肿瘤类型的定量荟萃分析结果；具体菌株与特定肿瘤类型的对应关系需参考其他实证研究。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群作为宿主可调节因素整合者的概念，以及其与免疫检查点抑制剂疗效异质性相关的证据。指出了微生物群受环境因素（饮食、药物等）高度影响（90%变异），这为解释为何生活方式干预可能影响免疫治疗提供了理论依据。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 可用于回答微生物群如何受外部因素影响从而间接调节ICIs疗效的背景部分；支持关于宿主因素在免疫治疗响应中重要性的论述。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制描述基于引用的早期小鼠研究和人类观察性研究，因果关系在人类中尚未完全确立；未详细说明短链脂肪酸如何具体调控T细胞或其他免疫细胞的功能细节。
facet_contributions.contribution: 描述了微生物群影响免疫反应的潜在机制路径：细菌发酵纤维产生短链脂肪酸 -> 滋养肠上皮细胞 -> 维持肠道黏膜屏障。这一机制解释了微生物群如何通过全身性炎症或免疫调节影响肿瘤微环境。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释微生物群介导效应的生物学机制部分，特别是关于代谢产物（SCFAs）和肠道屏障功能的部分。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文为综述提供了重要的概念框架和背景素材，主要价值在于确立了‘平行动物-人类研究’在能量平衡与癌症领域的应用范式，并详细阐述了肠道微生物群作为连接宿主可调节生活方式因素（饮食、运动等）与免疫检查点抑制剂疗效的关键中介角色。它不直接提供新的实验数据，而是汇总了现有证据的逻辑链条，特别适用于解释微生物群如何通过代谢产物（如短链脂肪酸）影响免疫微环境。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该论文为会议综述，其结论基于会议讨论和引用的文献，不代表作者原创的实验发现。
关于微生物群与免疫治疗响应的关联，文中提到的是‘新兴角色’和‘近期研究’，具体因果机制仍需结合更详细的实证研究进行验证。
提到的128名黑色素瘤患者研究仅为举例，不能代表所有固体肿瘤类型或所有免疫检查点抑制剂的效果。
微生物群遗传继承性仅占10%，其余90%由环境决定，这一比例强调了生活方式干预的潜力，但具体到个体差异的稳定性需谨慎解读。
topic_handles: energy balance components (physical activity, body composition, dietary intake)
gut microbiome modulation of immune checkpoint inhibitors
host modifiable factors (obesity, diet, exercise, stress, sleep)
short-chain fatty acids and gut mucosal barrier

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇会议综述，其综合路线是基于特定学术会议（Translating Energy Balance from Bench to Communities）的讨论内容进行的总结。作者汇集了来自不同学科（基础、临床、人口科学）的研究者的知识和成功案例，以梳理能量平衡各要素（物理活动、身体成分、饮食）在癌症全周期中的作用。文中引用的具体机制细节（如微生物群发酵纤维产生短链脂肪酸）来源于所讨论的相关研究文献，而非作者亲自进行的实验。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提出了在癌症研究中采用平行动物-人类研究的方法论框架，强调基础发现与临床观察的双向转化价值。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 作为会议综述，其内容依赖于会议讨论的范围和受邀讲者的观点，未提供系统性的文献检索流程或全面的元分析数据。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 整合了能量平衡要素（饮食、运动、身体成分）与癌症预后的关系，并特别突出了肠道微生物群在免疫治疗中的潜在作用。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 摘要未交代具体的统计综合方法或量化效应大小；对于微生物群介导的具体因果机制，仅引用了相关研究的结果，未在本综述中独立验证。

key_findings.conditions: 免疫检查点抑制剂治疗背景下
key_findings.finding: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂显著改善了多种癌症（如转移性黑色素瘤）的生存率，但约50%的患者无响应。宿主的可调节因素（肥胖、饮食、运动等）是决定肿瘤响应与抵抗的重要维度，其中肠道微生物群因受环境因素（90%变异由暴露决定）影响且能塑造免疫反应而受到关注。

key_findings.conditions: 动物模型与人类研究对比
key_findings.finding: 早期小鼠研究表明肠道微生物群影响免疫疗法反应，粪菌移植可传递这种反应性；人类研究则比较了响应者与未响应患者的肠道微生物群差异，近期研究进一步考察了可调节生活方式因素、微生物群与免疫疗法反应之间的相互作用。

key_findings.conditions: 机制层面
key_findings.finding: 与免疫疗法响应相关的细菌参与纤维的发酵和消化，产生短链脂肪酸，后者是肠上皮细胞的主要营养来源并有助于形成肠道黏膜屏障。一项涉及128名接受免疫检查点阻滞治疗的黑色素瘤患者的研究显示了对饮食、补充剂、抑郁焦虑症状和体力活动的调查。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 解决当前能量平衡与癌症研究中基础研究与临床研究脱节的问题，倡导通过平行动物-人类研究将知识转化为实践改变。同时，针对免疫检查点抑制剂疗效异质性的问题，探讨未被充分研究的宿主可调节因素（特别是肠道微生物群）的作用。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 该综述聚焦于能量平衡（包括体力活动、身体成分和饮食摄入）与癌症发展、癌症预后及健康生存之间的关系。研究情境基于2021年7月举行的“从实验室到社区的能量平衡转化：在癌症中应用平行动物-人类研究”会议，涉及基础科学、转化/临床科学和人口科学研究领域的调查者。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本文是一篇会议综述，旨在总结关于利用平行动物-人类研究来推进能量平衡与癌症研究的讨论。文章指出，以往的研究多在啮齿动物或患者群体中孤立进行，而通过平行研究（即动物模型指导临床/人群研究设计，或临床观察成为动物研究基础）可获得实质性益处。综述重点讨论了体力活动、身体成分和饮食摄入对癌症的影响，并特别引入了免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）作为背景，探讨了宿主可调节因素（如肥胖、饮食、运动、压力、睡眠和肠道微生物群）如何影响肿瘤对免疫治疗的反应。

source_materials.title: Translating energy balance research from the bench to the clinic to the community: Parallel animal-human studies in cancer

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 为综述建立“药物-微生物群-免疫反应”这一核心交互框架提供背景支持，说明为何需要关注合并用药。
broader_review_uses.material: 综述指出微生物群参与ICI复杂的作用机制，且药物相互作用可能破坏这种平衡。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 背景与概念框架

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 将微生物群研究的理论发现转化为临床决策的实际考量，展示该领域研究的实际应用价值。
broader_review_uses.material: 建议临床医生根据循证指南评估合并治疗的必要性，并讨论推迟ICI启动或转换策略。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 实践知识与临床相关性

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅基于综述汇总，未提供原始数据。对于证据不一致的药物，不能确定其对微生物群的具体改变方向或最终临床结局。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了关于特定药物类别（抗生素、PPIs、皮质类固醇）对ICI疗效负面影响的汇总证据，确认了它们通过破坏微生物群平衡从而降低疗效的现象。同时列出了其他可能影响疗效的药物清单（二甲双胍、他汀类等），尽管其临床证据不一致。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于支持“微生物群介导ICI疗效”这一论点中，关于外部因素（药物）如何破坏微生物群稳定性的部分。可用于列举导致疗效下降的具体临床场景。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 摘要未详细阐述“初始免疫致敏”的具体生物学定义或测量指标，也未说明药物干预如何具体阻断这一过程。
facet_contributions.contribution: 指出了“时间框架”作为关键变量，强调在ICI启动时保留“初始免疫致敏”的重要性。暗示药物干扰可能发生在特定的免疫激活窗口期。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于解释机制中的时序依赖性，即微生物群的改变或免疫系统的状态可能在治疗初期尤为敏感。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述直接关联“肠道微生物群”与“免疫检查点抑制剂”之间的相互作用，特别是通过药物干扰微生物群进而影响疗效这一路径。它为综述提供了关于哪些药物类别被广泛认为有害（抗生素、PPIs、皮质类固醇）以及哪些药物证据尚存争议（二甲双胍、他汀类等）的分类素材，有助于回答微生物群介导机制中的外部干扰因素部分。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该材料为综述性质，其发现的确定性依赖于其所引用的原始研究的质量和数据量。
对于二甲双胍、他汀类等药物，临床前与临床研究结果的差异提示情境依赖性，不能简单外推为普适结论。
摘要未提供具体的微生物群组成变化数据（如哪些菌属增加/减少），仅描述了药物对整体疗效的影响方向。
所给摘要未交代具体的文献筛选数量、数据库来源及偏倚风险评估细节。
topic_handles: Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) Impact on ICI Efficacy
Timing of ICI Initiation relative to Comedications
Clinical vs Preclinical Evidence Discrepancies in Drug-Microbiome-ICI Axis

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇综述，本研究通过编译已发表的关于微生物群在ICI疗效中的作用及合并用药影响的数据来进行综合。它并非进行新的实验研究，而是对现有临床前和临床研究数据进行整理和归纳，特别关注那些结论一致（如皮质类固醇、抗生素、PPIs的负面影响）与结论不一致（如二甲双胍、阿司匹林等）的药物类别。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了关于常见合并用药（特别是抗生素、PPIs、皮质类固醇）对ICI疗效负面影响的共识性总结；梳理了其他潜在有益或有害药物的现有证据状态（临床前vs临床）；提出了基于证据的治疗决策建议，包括评估必要性和考虑时间窗口。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索策略、纳入排除标准、质量评估方法或详细的统计综合过程。对于结论不一致的药物，未提供具体的异质性分析或解释为何临床研究与临床前结果存在差异的详细机制探讨。

key_findings.conditions: 皮质类固醇、抗生素、质子泵抑制剂
key_findings.finding: 主要发现结果一致，表明这些药物对ICI疗效具有破坏性/负面影响。

key_findings.conditions: 二甲双胍、阿司匹林、非甾体抗炎药、β受体阻滞剂、肾素-血管紧张素-醛固酮系统抑制剂、阿片类药物、他汀类药物
key_findings.finding: 在临床前模型中与改善或受损的ICI结果相关，但在回顾性临床研究中存在分歧/不一致的结论。

key_findings.conditions: ICI治疗的时间框架
key_findings.finding: 时间框架是一个重要变量，关键在于保留ICI启动时的初始免疫致敏（immune priming）。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 解决临床医生在面对ICIs合并用药时面临的矛盾信息问题，即在肿瘤反应与共病管理之间做出权衡。具体探讨微生物群如何介导这些药物相互作用，以及不同药物对ICI疗效的具体影响方向。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 固体肿瘤患者接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗期间，合并使用其他药物（comedications）对疗效的影响；重点涉及微生物群在其中的作用机制。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 该论文是一篇综述，旨在为临床医生提供关于ICIs合并用药影响的实用概览。文章分析了现有数据，指出大多数有害药物（如皮质类固醇、抗生素和质子泵抑制剂）会损害免疫疗法疗效，而某些分子（如二甲双胍、他汀类药物、阿司匹林等）在临床前模型中显示改善或损害结果，但在回顾性临床研究中结论不一致。综述强调了时间框架的重要性，建议临床医生根据循证指南评估合并治疗的必要性，并讨论推迟ICI启动或转换策略以保护关键窗口期。

source_materials.title: Comedications with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Involvement of the Microbiota, Impact on Efficacy and Practical Implications

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps contextualize why microbiome changes might broadly affect cancer biology beyond just immune therapy.
broader_review_uses.material: Summary of common pathways: chronic inflammation (LPS/TLR/NF-κB), genotoxicity (colibactin/nitrosamines), barrier dysfunction, and metabolic alterations (bile acids/SCFAs).
broader_review_uses.purpose: Background on shared mechanisms

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Provides context on the current state of clinical translation, noting that while promising, these are not yet standard care.
broader_review_uses.material: Discussion of FMT, probiotics, and dietary interventions as potential adjuncts to therapy, with caveats about their experimental status.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Examples of translational strategies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps structure the review by anatomical or mechanistic categories if needed.
broader_review_uses.material: Distinction between cancers with direct gut-tumor interaction (GI) vs those influenced by systemic immune/metabolic effects (Extra-GI).
broader_review_uses.purpose: Comparison of GI vs Extra-GI cancers

facet_contributions.boundaries: Associations are often derived from observational studies or murine models; causal direction in humans is not fully proven for all cancers. Clinical utility of profiling is stated as investigational.
facet_contributions.contribution: Lists specific microbial taxa associated with improved or impaired ICI response in 7 extra-GI cancers (Melanoma, Lung, Breast, Prostate, Brain, Cervical, Oral) and 6 GI cancers. For example, notes that Akkermansia and Bifidobacterium are linked to better ICI outcomes in Melanoma, HCC, and Lung Cancer, while Fusobacterium is linked to resistance in CRC.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to answer which microbes are consistently associated with ICI efficacy across different tumor types. Provides a comparative table (Table 1) summarizing these associations.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Many mechanistic details (e.g., specific signaling pathways like Wnt/β-catenin or FXR/TGR5) are described at a conceptual level; detailed molecular pathways for every taxon-cancer pair are not exhaustively covered.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details mechanisms by which microbes modulate immunity: beneficial taxa enhance antigen presentation and CD8+ T-cell activation; pathogenic taxa suppress NK cells, recruit MDSCs, or cause T-cell exhaustion. Also describes non-immune mechanisms like genotoxicity (colibactin) and metabolic disruption (bile acids) that create a pro-tumor environment affecting therapy.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Provides mechanistic explanations for *how* the microbiome affects therapy, distinguishing between direct immune modulation and indirect effects via inflammation or metabolism.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review serves as a high-level map of microbiome-cancer interactions, specifically valuable for identifying which microbial taxa and mechanisms are most strongly associated with Immunotherapy (ICI) efficacy across different solid tumors. It provides a structured comparison of 'beneficial' vs 'pathogenic' microbes for each cancer type, offering concrete examples of taxa (e.g., Akkermansia for responders, Fusobacterium for resistance) and mechanisms (immune priming vs. exhaustion) relevant to the facet questions.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic review with quantitative effect sizes. Associations should be treated as reported trends rather than definitive causal proofs.
Evidence for extra-GI cancers often relies on preclinical models or small observational studies; extrapolation to clinical practice requires caution.

The term 'gut microbiome' is used broadly to include oral and vaginal microbiomes in specific contexts (e.g., OSCC, Cervical Cancer); distinctions should be noted when applying to 'gut-specific' questions.
topic_handles: Microbial Taxa (Akkermansia muciniphila, Bifidobacterium, Fusobacterium nucleatum, etc.)
Mechanisms: Immune Modulation, Genotoxicity, Metabolism (Bile Acids, SCFAs)

study_summary_A.approach: Narrative synthesis of literature from PubMed and Web of Science (2004–2025). The authors qualitatively integrated findings from peer-reviewed studies providing mechanistic insights, clinical associations, or interventional evidence. No formal meta-analysis or risk-of-bias assessment was performed. The selection criteria for included cancers were based on the strength of mechanistic data linking microbial alterations to tumor outcomes and their global health burden.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive framework linking gut microbiome dysbiosis to both oncogenesis and therapeutic response across 13 distinct cancer types, highlighting shared mechanisms (inflammation, genotoxicity) and unique axes (e.g., gut-liver, gut-brain).
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a narrative review, it lacks quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis) and formal quality assessment. Evidence for many extra-GI cancers relies heavily on associative data or preclinical models, limiting direct clinical applicability.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Identifies specific microbial signatures (e.g., Akkermansia, Fusobacterium) as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI response and chemoresistance.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Clinical translation of microbiome profiling and modulation (FMT, probiotics) is currently limited to research settings; standardization and long-term safety are not yet established.

key_findings.conditions: Across GI and extra-GI cancers
key_findings.finding: Common mechanisms include pro-inflammatory signaling (NF-κB, STAT3), DNA damage from bacterial toxins (colibactin, nitrosating species), metabolite-driven promotion (secondary bile acids, TMAO), and barrier dysfunction.

key_findings.conditions: Immunotherapy (ICI) response in Melanoma, HCC, CRC, Lung Cancer
key_findings.finding: Higher microbial diversity and enrichment of specific taxa (Akkermansia muciniphila, Bifidobacterium longum, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii) correlate with improved ICI efficacy. Conversely, dysbiosis or antibiotic use is associated with reduced efficacy.

key_findings.conditions: Colorectal Cancer (CRC)
key_findings.finding: Fusobacterium nucleatum promotes progression via Wnt/β-catenin activation and immune suppression; also confers resistance to 5-FU and oxaliplatin.

key_findings.conditions: Gastric Cancer
key_findings.finding: Helicobacter pylori (CagA/VacA) is a Class I carcinogen causing DNA damage; dysbiosis with nitrosating bacteria exacerbates this.

key_findings.conditions: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC)
key_findings.finding: Gut-liver axis dysbiosis alters bile acid metabolism (FXR/TGR5 signaling) and increases LPS translocation, driving inflammation and fibrosis.

key_findings.conditions: Breast Cancer
key_findings.finding: Dysbiosis affects the estrobolome, altering estrogen metabolism; local bacteria may induce DNA breaks.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: To synthesize existing mechanistic and translational evidence linking the gut microbiome to both the development (oncogenesis) and treatment response (oncotherapies) of a broad spectrum of cancers, addressing the gap where prior reviews focused on individual cancers rather than systemic effects across multiple malignancies.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The review covers the role of the gut microbiome in oncogenesis and oncotherapies across thirteen cancer types: six gastrointestinal cancers (colorectal, gastric, hepatocellular, gallbladder, esophageal, pancreatic) and seven extra-gastrointestinal cancers (oral squamous cell carcinoma, cervical, prostate, breast, lung, brain tumors, melanoma). It focuses on mechanistic links to tumor initiation/progression and modulation of therapy responses, particularly immunotherapy.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on how gut microbial dysbiosis influences cancer development and treatment outcomes. The authors selected thirteen cancers based on robust mechanistic data and clinical relevance. They detail specific microbial taxa associated with each cancer type, outlining mechanisms such as chronic inflammation, genotoxicity, metabolic alterations, and immune modulation. The review highlights that while some microbes promote carcinogenesis through DNA damage or pro-inflammatory signaling, others support antitumor immunity. Crucially, it emphasizes the microbiome's role in modulating responses to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and especially immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), noting that beneficial taxa like Akkermansia muciniphila are linked to better ICI efficacy, whereas dysbiosis can lead to resistance. The paper concludes by discussing translational strategies like diet, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), cautioning that these remain largely investigational outside of clinical trials.

source_materials.title: Role of Gut Microbiome in Oncogenesis and Oncotherapies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 帮助读者建立肠道微生物群不仅是消化器官共生体，更是系统性免疫和代谢调节器的概念框架，这是理解其如何影响癌症免疫治疗的基础前提。
broader_review_uses.material: 摘要中关于肠道微生物群影响营养吸收、免疫系统及疾病反应的总体描述，以及菌群失调与糖尿病、肥胖、心血管疾病的关联。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 背景介绍：定义肠道微生物群在宿主健康中的基础角色，特别是其与代谢综合征的联系。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 提醒综述作者在讨论微生物干预时，需注意结果的异质性和菌株依赖性，避免过度概括。虽然本文未讨论ICIs，但其对“菌株特异性”的强调可应用于后续分析哪些菌种可能真正影响ICIs疗效。
broader_review_uses.material: 摘要中提到的“需要考虑菌株特异性效应和研究变异性”，以及益生元/益生菌在代谢健康中的潜在益处。
broader_review_uses.purpose: 概念区分：明确益生元/益生菌的一般作用与特定治疗情境下的差异。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 仅涉及代谢健康背景，未涉及肿瘤微环境或ICIs的具体相互作用。不能直接回答ICIs疗效受何种特定菌种调节的问题。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群失调与全身性低度炎症、代谢紊乱之间的基础关联背景。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 可用于解释为何肠道微生物状态可能间接影响全身免疫环境，从而为理解其对肿瘤微环境或系统免疫治疗的潜在背景影响提供生理学依据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 描述的是通用免疫机制，未指明这些机制在ICIs治疗背景下是否被特定菌群激活或抑制。需结合其他专门研究ICIs与微生物互作的论文来确定具体因果链条。
facet_contributions.contribution: 阐述了短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）和Toll样受体介导的免疫调节基本机制。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 可作为机制部分的背景知识，说明微生物代谢物如何一般性地调节免疫通路（抗炎/促炎平衡），这些基础机制可能是ICIs疗效调节的上游或并行路径。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述主要提供肠道微生物群基础生物学背景、代谢健康关联机制以及益生元/益生菌的一般性调节作用。对于用户关注的“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效”这一核心问题，本文不直接提供ICIs相关的实证数据或具体机制，但可作为理解肠道微生物群基础免疫调节环境（如低度炎症、屏障功能）的背景素材。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 本文是代谢健康领域的综述，未涉及实体瘤或免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）。
所有关于免疫调节的描述均为一般生理机制，未验证其在肿瘤免疫治疗中的具体表现。
作者强调的“菌株特异性”和“研究变异性”提示，任何将本文发现的益生菌益处外推到ICIs疗效预测时都需谨慎，必须依赖专门针对ICIs的研究证据。
topic_handles: strain-specific effects of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium

study_summary_A.approach: 文献综述与机制综合。作者整合了关于肠道微生物群生理学、代谢产物（如短链脂肪酸）的作用机制、免疫调节通路（包括Toll样受体和炎症途径）以及益生元/益生菌临床效应的现有知识。方法侧重于从生理机制角度结合临床视角进行理论梳理，而非执行新的实验研究。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群、代谢健康、益生元/益生菌之间关系的综合性生理机制概述，特别是关于短链脂肪酸和免疫通路的连接。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的检索策略、纳入排除标准或针对特定肿瘤免疫治疗（如ICIs）的分析。结论强调需要进一步研究以优化治疗潜力，表明当前证据尚不足以确立确定的临床指南。

key_findings.conditions: 肠道微生物群整体生态
key_findings.finding: 肠道微生物群是维持整体健康的关键动态生态系统，影响营养吸收、免疫系统和疾病反应；菌群失调与2型糖尿病、肥胖和心血管疾病等代谢障碍相关。

key_findings.conditions: 益生元摄入
key_findings.finding: 益生元滋养有益细菌并促进其生长，对肠道微生物群产生积极影响。

key_findings.conditions: 益生菌摄入（特别是乳杆菌和双歧杆菌菌株）
key_findings.finding: 可能改善代谢结局，如糖尿病患者的血糖控制，但效果具有菌株特异性，且存在研究变异性。

key_findings.conditions: 微生物发酵产物
key_findings.finding: 短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）调节抗炎和免疫系统通路； impaired gut barrier function, endotoxemia, and low-grade inflammation are associated with toll-like receptors influencing pro-inflammatory pathways.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 阐明肠道微生物群如何影响代谢健康，以及益生元和益生菌如何通过调节菌群组成和生理机制来改善或预防代谢性疾病。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）与代谢健康及疾病的关系，重点聚焦于益生元（prebiotics）和益生菌（probiotics）对肠道菌群组成、肠道屏障功能、免疫反应及代谢产物的调节作用。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 该论文是一篇综述报告，旨在回顾肠道微生物群在代谢健康和疾病中的作用，并评估益生元和益生菌对该微生物群的影响及其治疗潜力。文章阐述了肠道微生物作为动态生态系统对营养吸收、免疫系统和疾病反应的深远影响，特别指出了菌群失调（dysbiosis）与2型糖尿病、肥胖和心血管疾病等代谢紊乱的关联。文中详细描述了短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）通过调节抗炎和免疫通路发挥作用的机制，以及 Toll 样受体介导的低度炎症途径。同时，文章强调了特定菌株（如乳杆菌和双歧杆菌）在改善血糖控制等方面的潜在益处，并指出在解读结果时需考虑菌株特异性效应和研究变异性。

source_materials.title: Understanding How Pre- and Probiotics Affect the Gut Microbiome and Metabolic Health.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps structure the review to distinguish between systemic (gut-derived) and local (lung-resident) microbial effects on immunotherapy.
broader_review_uses.material: The study explicitly contrasts its findings with the well-known gut microbiome-ICI relationship, highlighting the unique 'private identification card' nature of the lower respiratory tract microbiome.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextual comparison with gut microbiome literature

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Provides a methodological example for assessing local tumor microenvironment microbiomes in accessible sites, relevant for reviews discussing biomarker discovery strategies.
broader_review_uses.material: Demonstrates the feasibility of using BALF for multi-omics (16S, metabolomics) and immune profiling in NSCLC patients.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Methodological reference for non-invasive sampling

facet_contributions.boundaries: Limited to advanced NSCLC; small cohort (n=26); retrospective association only.
facet_contributions.contribution: Identifies specific lower respiratory tract microbial taxa associated with ICI response in NSCLC: Bacillus enrichment correlates with positive response, while Sphingomonas and Sediminibacterium correlate with progression. Demonstrates that beta-diversity of the lung microbiome is a significant discriminator of clinical outcome.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Use to support arguments that site-specific microbiomes (lung vs. gut) have distinct predictive values. Can be cited as evidence for 'protective' vs 'detrimental' microbial signatures in solid tumors outside the GI tract.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Mechanistic links are correlative (multi-omics integration); causality not proven. Does not isolate specific metabolites or test functional effects directly.
facet_contributions.contribution: Proposes a mechanism where microbiome-derived metabolites (lipid and amino acid metabolism pathways) reshape the local immune microenvironment. Specifically, beneficial microbes promote the release of cytokines (IL-1β, MCP-1, IL-8) that recruit CD8+ T cells and M1 macrophages, enhancing anti-tumor immunity.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Illustrates a concrete mechanism of microbiome-host interaction in the lung context. Useful for discussing how local microbial metabolism influences immune cell infiltration and function, complementing gut-based mechanisms.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This paper offers critical evidence that the lower respiratory tract microbiome, independent of the gut, modulates ICI efficacy in NSCLC through local metabolic-immune crosstalk. It provides specific microbial markers (Bacillus as beneficial, Sphingomonas/Sediminibacterium as detrimental) and mechanistic insights involving lipid/amino acid metabolism and cytokine-mediated CD8+ T cell/M1 macrophage recruitment. This supports the broader review's inclusion of site-specific microbiomes beyond the gut.
scope_interpretation_cautions: Do not generalize findings to all solid tumors; this is specific to advanced NSCLC.
The study does not establish causality; associations are observed in a retrospective cohort.
Gut microbiome data is absent; do not infer lung-gut axis interactions from this paper alone.
Sample size is small (n=26); results should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive predictive models.

study_summary_A.approach: Retrospective observational study. Cohort: 26 advanced NSCLC patients treated with anti-PD-1 monotherapy, categorized into Responders (PR+SD, n=17) and Non-Responders (PD, n=11), excluding those with recent antibiotic use or other infections. Samples: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) for 16S rRNA sequencing (V3-V4 region) and untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics; paired serum and BALF for LEGENDplex immunoassays of inflammatory cytokines/chemokines; tumor tissues for multiplex immunofluorescence staining (CD4, CD8, CD68, CD206). Analysis: Alpha/Beta diversity metrics, LEfSe for differential taxa, O2PLS and CCA for microbe-metabolite integration, ROC curves for predictive modeling, and correlation analyses linking microbes/metabolites to cytokine levels and immune cell infiltration.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides the first detailed multi-omics landscape (microbiome + metabolome + immune profile) of the lower respiratory tract in advanced NSCLC patients undergoing ICI therapy, identifying specific microbial signatures (Bacillus vs. Sphingomonas/Sediminibacterium) associated with clinical outcomes.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Small sample size (n=26) limits statistical power and generalizability. Retrospective design and single-center origin introduce selection bias. Lack of longitudinal sampling before treatment initiation restricts causal inference regarding microbial changes. Gut microbiome data was not collected, preventing assessment of the lung-gut axis interactions.

key_findings.conditions: Comparing Responders (PR/SD) vs. Non-Responders (PD) in advanced NSCLC.
key_findings.finding: Microbial diversity (beta diversity) significantly differed between groups, with Responders showing distinct community structures. Bacillus was enriched in Responders, while Sphingomonas and Sediminibacterium were associated with Non-Responders.

key_findings.conditions: Metabolomic profiling of BALF.
key_findings.finding: Responders exhibited metabolic profiles favoring lipid metabolism and essential amino acid degradation pathways linked to beneficial microbes. Non-Responders showed alterations in these pathways associated with pathogenic genera.

key_findings.conditions: Immune microenvironment analysis (Tissue & Fluids).
key_findings.finding: Responders had higher infiltration of CD8+ T cells and M1 macrophages (CD68+/CD206-) in tumors. BALF from Responders showed elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, MCP-1, IL-8) compared to Non-Responders, correlating with microbial markers.

key_findings.conditions: Predictive modeling.
key_findings.finding: A multi-component model combining specific microbes, metabolites, and cytokines (e.g., IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-α2) demonstrated potential for predicting ICI response, though validation is limited by sample size.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: While the gut microbiome's role in ICI response is well-documented, the specific microecological features and predictive value of the lower respiratory tract microbiome in advanced NSCLC remain unclear. This study seeks to determine if local microbial dysbiosis correlates with ICB efficacy and to uncover the underlying metabolic and immune mechanisms.
study_summary_A.research_scope: Advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy; focus on lower respiratory tract microbiome and metabolome via bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF).
study_summary_A.work_summary: This study investigates the role of the lower respiratory tract microbiome in predicting clinical responses to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in advanced NSCLC. Using a retrospective single-center cohort of 26 patients, the authors performed 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics on BALF samples, alongside cytokine/chemokine assays and multiplex immunohistochemistry on tissue biopsies. The research aims to identify microbial and metabolic signatures associated with treatment outcomes (Partial Response/Stable Disease vs. Progressive Disease) and elucidate the mechanisms by which local microbes influence the tumor immune microenvironment.

source_materials.title: Lower respiratory tract microbiome dysbiosis impairs clinical responses to immune checkpoint blockade in advanced non‐small‐cell lung cancer

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Contextualizes ICI efficacy within host factors and comorbidities.
broader_review_uses.material: Discusses how NASH, viral etiology (HBV/HCV), age, BMI, and sarcopenia affect ICI outcomes.
broader_review_uses.purpose: To highlight that host background and comorbidities significantly modulate ICI response, providing a broader view of factors beyond just the tumor or microbiome.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Links toxicity to efficacy.
broader_review_uses.material: Summarizes conflicting evidence on whether irAEs predict better survival.
broader_review_uses.purpose: To discuss the complex relationship between immune activation (manifested as toxicity) and therapeutic benefit, which is relevant to understanding immune-mediated mechanisms.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Findings are mixed; some studies show no association. Evidence is primarily from HCC, not all solid tumors. Causality is not established; most data are observational.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details specific gut microbiota taxa (Prevotella 9, Lachnoclostridium, Veillonella, Akkermansia) associated with ICI response in HCC. Reports that antibiotic use is linked to shorter PFS/OS in some studies, suggesting microbiome modulation affects efficacy.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to illustrate how gut microbiome composition and external perturbations (antibiotics) influence ICI efficacy in a solid tumor context. Provides specific bacterial names and metabolites (ursodeoxycholic acid) for mechanistic discussion.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Mechanisms are largely hypothesized or derived from preclinical/small studies. Direct causal links between specific microbes and ICI mechanism in HCC are not fully elucidated. No direct evidence for general solid tumor mechanisms.
facet_contributions.contribution: Proposes mechanisms linking microbiome to immunity: mentions loss of antitumor CD4+ T cells and accumulation of exhausted CD8+ T cells in NASH-HCC; suggests bile acids as mediators. Links irAEs to immune homeostasis disruption.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Offers hypotheses on mechanisms (T-cell exhaustion, bile acid signaling) that could mediate microbiome-ICI interactions. Can be cited as potential pathways to investigate further.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review provides a broad landscape of biomarkers influencing ICI efficacy in HCC, with specific sections on gut microbiome and irAEs that are directly relevant to the review's focus on mechanisms and modulation of ICI response. It offers concrete examples of microbial associations and antibiotic impacts, which can be used to discuss environmental/host factors modulating ICI efficacy in solid tumors.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review focuses on HCC; findings regarding microbiome and host factors may not be directly generalizable to all solid tumors without caution.
Many biomarker associations are based on retrospective studies with potential confounding; causality should not be inferred.
Conflicting results exist for key markers (e.g., antibiotics, PD-L1, TMB); do not present any single finding as definitive consensus.
topic_handles: antibiotic use impact on ICI efficacy
immune-related adverse events (irAEs) as surrogate for efficacy
viral etiology (HBV vs HCV vs non-viral)

study_summary_A.approach: The authors conducted a narrative review by synthesizing data from various clinical trials (Phase I-III), retrospective and prospective observational studies, and meta-analyses. They organized the literature into specific categories of biomarkers (biochemical, cellular, tumor-related, imaging, etiological, microbiome, and safety-related) and summarized their predictive value for outcomes such as overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR).

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive categorization of diverse biomarkers (serum, cellular, tumor, host, microbiome) for ICI efficacy in HCC, serving as a reference for clinical trial design and biomarker discovery.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Most included studies are retrospective with small sample sizes; lack of standardized protocols for novel biomarkers (ctDNA, microbiome); conflicting results for several markers (PD-L1, TMB, antibiotics); insufficient prospective validation for many candidates.

key_findings.conditions: Baseline serum markers
key_findings.finding: Low baseline AFP (<400 µg/L) and low CRAFITY score (combining AFP and CRP) are associated with better OS and PFS. Low ALBI score indicates preserved liver function and predicts better survival. High IL-6 and TGF-b levels correlate with poor response.

key_findings.conditions: Peripheral blood cell indices
key_findings.finding: Low NLR (<5), low PLR, high PNI, and low MLR/CII/SIRI are generally associated with improved OS and PFS. Early changes in monocyte subsets (e.g., CD14+/CD16+) also show predictive potential.

key_findings.conditions: Tumor-related molecular markers
key_findings.finding: PD-L1 expression shows inconsistent predictive value in HCC. TMB has limited utility due to low mutation burden in HCC. ctDNA clearance and low baseline cfDNA levels correlate with better outcomes. CTCs with PD-L1 expression have conflicting results regarding response prediction.

key_findings.conditions: Clinical and host factors
key_findings.finding: Splenomegaly and sarcopenia (low SMI) are associated with poorer prognosis. Older age (≥65 years) may respond better to ICIs. HBV-related HCC tends to have better outcomes than non-viral or HCV-related HCC. NASH-related HCC shows poorer response.

key_findings.conditions: Gut microbiome
key_findings.finding: Specific microbial compositions (e.g., enrichment of Lachnoclostridium, Veillonella; absence of Prevotella 9) correlate with better response. Antibiotic use during treatment is associated with shorter PFS and OS in some studies, though results are conflicting.

key_findings.conditions: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs)
key_findings.finding: Some studies suggest irAEs (especially grade ≥3) correlate with better survival, but other large studies found no significant difference. CRAFITY score may predict lower incidence of severe irAEs.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: To identify reliable prognostic biomarkers that can predict the efficacy of ICIs treatment in HCC patients, thereby enabling optimal patient selection to maximize clinical benefits while minimizing unnecessary toxic side effects and economic losses.
study_summary_A.research_scope: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 and anti-CTLA-4 agents, often in combination with targeted therapies or other modalities.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This review systematically categorizes and summarizes current evidence on biomarkers predicting the efficacy of ICIs in HCC. It covers a wide range of indicators including serum/cellular markers (e.g., AFP, ALBI, NLR, cytokines), tumor-related markers (e.g., PD-L1, TMB, ctDNA, CTCs), clinical/imaging features (e.g., splenomegaly, sarcopenia, BMI), etiology (HBV/HCV/NASH), gut microbiome, and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The paper aims to guide future biomarker exploration and clinical decision-making by highlighting promising candidates and identifying areas requiring further validation through larger prospective studies.

source_materials.title: Biomarkers predicting the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in hepatocellular carcinoma

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Useful for discussing the historical inconsistency in the field and the importance of methodological rigor in microbiome research.
broader_review_uses.material: The paper critiques previous studies for using variable pipelines and small samples, leading to inconsistent results. It demonstrates how standardization reveals stronger NR signals.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextualize the evolution of microbiome biomarker discovery

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Highlights challenges in cross-study comparison and the need for standardized clinical annotations in future trials.
broader_review_uses.material: Discussion of varying response criteria (RECIST vs irRC), undefined Stable Disease (SD) categories, and regional differences in baseline microbiota (Bacteroides vs Prevotella).
broader_review_uses.purpose: Provide examples of technical limitations in microbiome-ICI studies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Supports the view that baseline microbiome composition is a key determinant of response, rather than treatment-induced changes alone.
broader_review_uses.material: Longitudinal analysis showed no significant beta diversity shifts during treatment.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Illustrate the stability of the microbiome during ICI therapy

facet_contributions.boundaries: Findings are based on retrospective reanalysis; causal mechanisms are not established. Performance varies by tumor type (e.g., weaker in NSCLC validation).
facet_contributions.contribution: Identifies specific bacterial species and OTUs consistently associated with ICI non-response (NR) across multiple cohorts, including Veillonella parvula, Bacteroides spp., and Clostridium spp. Also identifies responder-associated species like Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and novel ones like Roseburia hominis.
